expectations.text: Recommends the direct-to-speaker interview model rather than the organiser brokering every slot, citing DEF CON's practice of telling reporters to contact speakers directly.
expectations.evidence: "Brokering is acceptable"; it only describes DEF CON as the community norm and leaves the choice to the user.

expectations.text: States the two things that still belong to the organiser under the direct model: telling the reporter which speakers agreed to be contacted, and telling those speakers a reporter may contact them.
expectations.evidence: "A list of which speakers have agreed to be contacted" and "A notice to each speaker that a reporter may contact them."

expectations.text: Routes the speaker's own consent and pre-event cadence to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-speaker-experience.
expectations.evidence: "Speaker consent and pre-event cadence belong to your speaker-experience skill, so hand that part there."

expectations.text: Ranks a named contact plus a written recording rule above a working corner, on the grounds that a table with power does not stop a camera and a written rule does.
expectations.evidence: Says "A working corner on its own carries no rule" and justifies the room, with no ranking.

expectations.text: Produces a written shooting rule with four published parts, before doors.
expectations.evidence: Item 5 lists the four parts, "publish it with the accreditation policy".
